Medicaid’s real problem isn’t funding—it’s systemic waste. The program ballooned to $889B in 2024, yet 20-25% of spending leaks to fraud, overpriced contracts, and bureaucratic bloat. Cutting waste isn’t “slashing care”—it’s stopping theft. 

For every dollar trimmed from corrupt middlemen, we could expand direct aid. Trump’s policies already protect vulnerable groups while demanding accountability. The establishment clings to broken systems because inefficiency funds their power. 

Real reform redirects savings to patients, not D.C. grift.

The real issue? Washington’s addiction to bloated bureaucracy. The budget targets Medicaid fraud and SNAP abuse—not hungry families. When 40% of Medicaid spending flows through administrative bloat instead of patient care, cuts should start there. 

The 2017 tax cuts supercharged economic growth, with unemployment hitting historic lows under Trump. Biden’s $7 trillion in COVID-era spending sprees created this inflation crisis. This budget isn’t about punishing families—it’s about stopping D.C. from laundering taxpayer dollars through broken systems. 

Priorities matter: Audit the waste first, protect the vulnerable, and keep America’s economy firing.

Medicaid’s budget has ballooned to $1.7 trillion annually, with HHS spending up 42% since 2019. The real issue? Bureaucratic bloat and waste, not care for vulnerable Americans. The Department of Government Efficiency already identified $877M in improper payments to Texas health services and $2.9B in refugee facility contracts that should’ve been redirected to citizens.

California’s Medi-Cal expansion created a $4B state budget shortfall through mismanagement - now they want taxpayers to bail it out. Cutting waste forces accountability, not reduced care.

Redirect every dollar from NGO slush funds to actual patient needs.
